landmarks: the stone clock tower of Zagora
wildlife: cicadas singing in the chestnut trees
owls in the old plane trees
plants: old plane trees over the village squares
wild oregano and sage on the hillsides
activities: riding the little steam train through the forest
walking the old cobblestone mule paths between villages
swimming at a pebble cove below the mountain
eating spoon sweets on a shaded village square
watching fishing boats come into a tiny harbour
history: Greek myths say centaurs — half man, half horse — lived wild in Pelion's forests
the wise centaur Chiron, who taught the hero Achilles, is said to have lived on this mountain
villages here grew rich on silk and trade in the 1700s, which is why their mansions are so grand
the little steam train was built over a hundred years ago to link the mountain villages to the sea
stone paths called kalderimia once carried mules loaded with goods between every village
local_food: spoon sweets made from local fruit
fresh fish from the Pagasetic Gulf
weather: cool and green in summer compared to the coast below
golden and crisp in autumn, chestnut season
sometimes snowy on the mountain top in winter
interesting_facts: Greek myth says this mountain was home to the centaurs, and to Chiron, the gentle centaur who taught heroes.
Pelion has two very different coastlines: calm pebble coves on one side, and open sea on the other.
The old steam train is nicknamed 'Moutzouris', which means 'the sooty one', because of its smoke.
Villages here have grand old mansions from a time when the silk trade made Pelion wealthy.
The stone paths connecting the villages are so old that they were once the only roads on the mountain.
